clue.text: Gasping about first piece of incredible work of art

indicators.note: the first piece of a word is its opening letter alone
about means surrounding, so one word wraps around the other piece

blocks.note: gasping for breath is panting
the first piece of incredible is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone gasps in awe at an astonishing artwork.
explanation.definitionFit: A painting is a picture made with pigments, one of the most familiar kinds of artistic creation.

clue.text: Old insecticide is put in two targets for golfer

indicators.note: something put in another thing sits inside it, here between two words

blocks.note: par is the score a golfer aims at on a hole
taken as written
the green is the area a golfer aims the approach shot at

explanation.surface: A golfer's twin aims are oddly linked to a vintage pest killer.
explanation.walkthrough: The two golfing targets are par and the green; IS slips between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Paris green is a toxic copper arsenite compound formerly sprayed on crops to kill pests.

clue.text: Fish's brainwave cut short

indicators.note: cutting something short trims off its final letter

blocks.note: a brainwave is a sudden bright idea

explanation.surface: A fish's flash of inspiration gets interrupted.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for is, joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The ide is a European freshwater species of the carp family, also called the orfe.

clue.text: Vacancy retracted by play's writer

indicators.note: something retracted is pulled back, so the word runs in the opposite direction

blocks.note: a slot is an opening or vacancy, as in a free slot in a schedule
to toy with something is to play with it

explanation.surface: A theatre job vacancy is withdrawn by the playwright.
explanation.definitionFit: Leo Tolstoy was the Russian novelist who wrote War and Peace and Anna Karenina.

clue.text: Surprisingly rational men stealing a substance with tiny particles

indicators.note: stealing means taking something and keeping it inside, so the letters are held within
a surprising outcome is unexpected, so the letters come out in an unexpected order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Sensible scientists unexpectedly pilfer a microscopic substance.
explanation.definitionFit: Nanomaterials are engineered substances whose structure is measured in billionths of a metre.

clue.text: Like to take grandma fruit

indicators.note: to take something in is to hold it inside, so one piece encloses the other

blocks.note: as in the sense of like, similar to
nana is a familiar name for a grandmother

explanation.surface: Someone would like to bring their grandmother some fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: Like looks like a verb of wanting, but it means similar to; to take is the wrapping signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Ananas is the French and botanical name for the pineapple, the tropical plant and its fruit.

clue.text: Drink gin or generic drinks from the south

indicators.note: drinks means swallows up, so the phrase has the word absorbed inside it
in a down clue, reading from the south means reading upwards, against the normal direction

blocks.note: the letters straddle the words from gin to generic

explanation.surface: A cocktail fan sips gin or a cheaper own-brand version from somewhere southern.
explanation.definitionFit: A Negroni is an Italian cocktail of gin, Campari and sweet vermouth in equal parts.

clue.text: Myopic Spooner's fortune teller given honour

indicators.note: the Oxford don known for swapping the opening sounds of neighbouring words, so his version trades them

blocks.note: a seer foretells the future; taking the N noise from the next word, it is spelt this way
someone knighted has been honoured by the monarch; taking the S noise, it is spelt this way

explanation.surface: Spooner describes a clairvoyant who has received a royal honour.
explanation.walkthrough: Say seer knighted aloud and trade the opening sounds: the silent K in knighted leaves an N noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Myopia is the eye condition where distant things blur while close objects stay clear.

clue.text: What I do, reportedly, in burrow

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so we go by how it is said

blocks.note: the speaker is the crossword's setter, whose job is to set puzzles

explanation.surface: The setter describes their daily work from inside an animal's den.
explanation.walkthrough: I is the setter speaking, so what I do is set.
explanation.definitionFit: A sett is the underground tunnel system where a family of badgers lives.

clue.text: Wine and fish with chips following shot

indicators.note: to be shot of something is to be rid of it, so a letter is dropped

blocks.note: fries is the American word for chips
F is the standard abbreviation for following, and it is the letter removed
ling is a long-bodied sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A pub order: wine, then fish and chips after a quick shot.
explanation.walkthrough: Fish and chips leads you to expect a menu; the chips are fries with F removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Riesling is a white grape variety from the Rhine region and the aromatic white made from it.

clue.text: Shocked military commanders and leader in Turkey

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: an agha or aga was a commander in the Ottoman army
the opening letter of Turkey

explanation.surface: Turkish generals and their country's ruler are horrified by events.
explanation.definitionFit: Aghast describes someone filled with horror or amazement, a strong synonym for appalled.

clue.text: Opening lesson about overdose's not succeeded

indicators.note: not means take away, and succeeded is a letter the word loses
about means around, so the lesson word goes around the other piece

blocks.note: instruction is teaching, as in a lesson
S is the abbreviation for succeeded in family trees
OD is the usual short form of overdose

explanation.surface: A first class on drug overdoses has been a failure.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's reads as has: the lesson has lost S, then wraps around OD.
explanation.definitionFit: An introduction is the opening part of a book, speech or piece of music, preceding the main body.

clue.text: Smug cosmonaut is in base

indicators.note: base means debased or corrupt, so the letters are spoilt into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A self-satisfied Russian spaceman lounges at the launch base.
explanation.walkthrough: In base looks like a location for the cosmonaut, but in is fodder and base is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanctimonious describes a self-righteous person who parades moral superiority, matching a complacent, self-satisfied manner.

clue.text: Tied down? Then kiss

blocks.note: to neck a drink is to down it quickly
and can mean then, next in sequence
to neck is to kiss and cuddle, British informal

explanation.surface: A romantic scene: someone is tied down, then kissed.
explanation.walkthrough: Down is a verb meaning swallow, not the direction; necking is British slang for both gulping a drink and smooching.
explanation.definitionFit: Racers running neck and neck are exactly level, with neither ahead, so the contest is a draw so far.

clue.text: Sign seen in grocers' apropos the bananas

indicators.note: bananas means crazy, so the letters go wild and rearrange

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A notice in a greengrocer's shop about its bananas.
explanation.walkthrough: The grocer's apostrophe is the famous misplaced mark on shop signs like banana's; the clue itself contains one in grocers'.
explanation.definitionFit: The punctuation mark showing possession appears in grocers', and is notoriously misused on greengrocers' price cards.

clue.text: Precipitous shooting in Philadelphia that led to a spate of similar shootings

definitions.text: shooting in Philadelphia that led to a spate of similar shootings

blocks.note: first meaning: steep and full of crags

blocks.clueFragment: shooting in Philadelphia that led to a spate of similar shootings
blocks.note: second meaning: the boxing film made in that city, followed by many sequels

explanation.walkthrough: Shooting sounds like gunfire, but it is filming: the 1976 Stallone boxing movie was shot in Philadelphia and spawned a string of sequels.
explanation.definitionFit: Steep, craggy terrain is rugged and stony, and the film title names the boxer Rocky Balboa.

clue.text: Improving the appearance of dog, ass and rodent in the mirror

indicators.note: a mirror image is flipped, so the string of words reads backwards

blocks.note: a pug is a small flat-faced dog
an ass is a fool, and nit is British slang for a fool
a rat is a rodent

explanation.surface: Animals preen in front of a mirror to look smarter.
explanation.walkthrough: Tarting up is British informal for making something look showier.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarting up means smartening or decorating something, often cheaply, to make it look more attractive.

clue.text: Demeanour changes in love

indicators.note: when something changes it takes a new form, so the letters take a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone's whole manner alters when they fall for somebody.
explanation.definitionFit: Enamoured means smitten with or charmed by another person, filled with romantic feeling.

clue.text: Former pupil's treatment is not widely known

blocks.note: OB is old boy, a former pupil of a British school
taken as written
a cure is a medical treatment

explanation.surface: An old school alumnus's remedy turns out to be little known.
explanation.definitionFit: Something obscure is unfamiliar, recondite or little heard of by the general public.

clue.text: Make disapproving noise at American skirts

blocks.note: to tut is to click the tongue in disapproval
US stands for the United States, hence American

explanation.surface: Someone clicks their tongue at an American's short skirts.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutu is the short stiff frilly skirt worn by ballet dancers.

clue.text: Barrage of suffering when Republican displaces millions

indicators.note: to displace something is to push it out and take its place

blocks.note: torment is great suffering
R is the usual abbreviation for Republican
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: Political anguish as a Republican ousts a billionaire class.
explanation.walkthrough: R takes the place of M in the word for suffering.
explanation.definitionFit: A torrent is an overwhelming outpouring, as in a torrent of abuse, like a barrage of insults.

clue.text: Courier predicts hair dryer's cap is broken

indicators.note: a cap sits on top, so it is the opening letter of the word before it
something broken is smashed into pieces that can be put back in a different order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
the top letter of dryer

explanation.surface: Someone forecasts that the hood on their hair dryer is going to break.
explanation.walkthrough: Hair dryer looks like one item, but hair is fodder and only the first letter of dryer joins it.
explanation.definitionFit: A dispatch rider is a messenger on a motorcycle who delivers urgent documents and parcels.

clue.text: Cheese fondue, primarily with Greek character

indicators.note: primarily means in the first place, so just the opening letter is used

blocks.note: the opening letter of fondue
eta is the seventh letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A cheese fondue made mainly with Greek flavour.
explanation.definitionFit: Feta is the crumbly white brined Greek variety made from sheep or goat milk.

clue.text: Fizzy drink losing bit of sparkle in Settle

indicators.note: a bit of a word is a small piece, here its first letter
losing something means it is taken away from the whole

blocks.note: 7 Up is a lemon-lime soft drink brand
the opening letter of sparkle, which is dropped

explanation.surface: A soft drink goes flat in Settle, a town in North Yorkshire.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital S makes Settle look like the Yorkshire town, but it is the verb defining the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To even up a score or debt is to make it equal, squaring or balancing accounts.

clue.text: Got rid of electronic device producing dangerous gas

blocks.note: to fire someone is to get rid of them from a job
an amp is an amplifier

explanation.surface: Discarding an old gadget releases a hazardous gas.
explanation.definitionFit: Firedamp is the explosive methane gas found in coal mines, a major historic danger to miners.

clue.text: Bristle, as lake disappearing from grassy area

indicators.note: something disappearing from a place is removed from it

blocks.note: L is the map abbreviation for lake
a lawn is an area of mown grass

explanation.surface: Someone bristles as a lake dries up beside the grass.
explanation.walkthrough: Bristle looks like a verb of annoyance, but it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: An awn is the stiff hair-like projection on the seed head of barley, oats and other grasses.

clue.text: American taking year off allowed ornament

indicators.note: taking a thing off means removing it from the word

blocks.note: Yank is informal for an American
Y is the abbreviation for year
let means allowed

explanation.surface: An American on a year's leave is permitted some jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: An anklet is a chain or bracelet worn around the lower leg as decorative jewellery.

clue.text: Ready to receive delivery, for example

blocks.note: first meaning, split in two: a cricket batter set in position, waiting for the ball
second meaning: a case or specimen

explanation.walkthrough: Delivery sounds like a parcel, but in cricket a delivery is a ball bowled; a batter waiting for it is in stance.
explanation.definitionFit: An instance is a single case cited to illustrate a point, just like a specimen or illustration.
